_comment: Accuracy gates for the RF-DETR pipeline. `video` is a path to a local file (absolute, or relative to the repo root); `gt` names a per-frame ground-truth file in eval/gt/. Gates are IDENTITY gates over that ground truth, because aggregate KPIs can be right for the wrong reasons — a pipeline that follows the teacher for half a lesson and a look-alike for the other half still reports a plausible teacher_present_ms.

demo_teacher.label: Demo lesson (4:46, ~30 pupils, teacher in a dark kurta) — the room the previous pipeline found hardest
demo_teacher.note: The previous (YOLO + appearance-merge + tracklet-DP) pipeline scored 76.5% coverage / 83.7% purity here, and this room was the one that exposed its tuning as room-specific. RF-DETR measures 95.7% / 97.4%. Gates sit just under the measured values so they catch regressions rather than failing permanently.
demo_teacher.annotation_ceiling: The residual disagreements are GROUND-TRUTH errors, not pipeline errors — all 25 were dumped and three were pixel-verified against the video. Every one is an anchor whose box is a <9%-wide sliver pinned to the exact frame edge (x=0.000 or x+w=1.000), where the colour cue that built this ground truth cannot support a judgement. At 149.0s the anchor sits on a student's shoulder at the right edge while the teacher stands mid-frame and is detected correctly; at 215.2s the anchor sits on a student at the left edge while the teacher is out of shot entirely and the pipeline correctly says nothing. So the true accuracy is HIGHER than these gates record, and id_switches=3 is a count of annotation artifacts. This matches the harness critique already recorded in docs/teacher-identification-research.md: the colour oracle digs holes, and measured purity is plausibly inside its own labelling noise. Re-annotating with track-level human labels is the fix; until then, treat these numbers as a floor and do not tune against the last two points.
